analysis.investment_thesis: Bandhan Bank's forward P/E of ~11x looks superficially cheap for a recovering microfinance-heavy bank, but at ₹28,107 Cr market cap it is 14-28x outside my SMILE universe, promoter holding is only 39.74%, and the core MFI book still carries structural asset-quality fragility. This is a large-cap banking recovery trade, not a SMILE multibagger.
key_strengths: Net profit recovering strongly: ₹126 Cr (FY22) → ₹2,745 Cr (FY25) as NPA cycle normalises
P/B of 1.14x with ROE of 11% — balance sheet reasonably priced if earnings recovery sustains
Significant CASA franchise and strong brand recall in eastern India's unbanked/underbanked segments
key_risks: MFI book concentration — repeat asset quality stress during macro/weather shocks (FY22 was nearly a wipeout with ₹126 Cr profit)
Finance cost CAGR of 26.6% outpacing revenue CAGR of 7.8% — net interest margin compression risk
Promoter below 50% (39.74%) and RBI regulatory overhang on promoter dilution timeline
red_flags: Market cap ₹28,107 Cr — 14-28x outside my SMILE sweet spot; this is a large-cap bank
Promoter holding 39.74% — fails my minimum 50% threshold decisively
OCF was -₹4,245 Cr in FY23 — banking cash flows are inherently volatile and hard to underwrite
Current P/E of 27.92x is not cheap; forward P/E recovery depends on earnings normalisation that MFI stress could derail again
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bandhan's story is a cautionary tale wrapped inside a recovery narrative. The FY22 near-wipeout (₹126 Cr net profit on ₹11,536 Cr revenue) exposed the extreme vulnerability of an MFI-heavy model to COVID disruption and subsequent collection deterioration. The recovery to ₹2,745 Cr in FY25 is real and reflects gradual portfolio diversification into secured retail loans, home loans, and SME — but the transition is slow and the eastern India geographical concentration remains a systemic risk.

From the SMILE lens, there is nothing to like here as a new entry. Size (₹28K Cr) eliminates information asymmetry. Promoter holding at 39.74% means the founding shareholder has been forced to dilute significantly under RBI's promoter-cap regulations. Revenue growth of 7.8% CAGR over 3 years is below my 15-30% hurdle. I would need to see market cap below ₹5,000 Cr, promoter holding above 50%, and a differentiated liability franchise before even beginning my analysis — none of these are present.
